observed_title: On Jump Measures of Optional Processes with Regulated Trajectories
version: arXiv:1508.01973v1, 2015-08-09, 11 PDF pages; no later publication/version independently checked.

read_ranges.scope: entire extracted article: process measurability preliminaries, stopping-time enumeration for cadlag jumps, jump-measure construction/integration, Levy special case, regulated optional-process extension, all proofs, open problems and references

topic_relevance.J05: direct component source for enumerating jump times and representing the induced jump measure of an optional process with regulated trajectories. The theorem does not construct a compensator, a nonhomogeneous intensity kernel, or a frozen-coordinate iteration; those interface fields remain undefined.
topic_relevance.I02: adjacent: The preliminaries distinguish predictable, optional, progressive and adapted processes, and the paper constructs the induced jump random measure; it does not develop optional/predictable projection or a general compensator.

definitions.name: regulated optional process and jump set
definitions.statement: Under the usual conditions on the filtration, an optional process X with regulated trajectories has X− predictable and X+ adapted; the jump process ΔX=X+−X− is optional. The trajectory jump set is at most countable and is partitioned into finite subsets by bounded time windows and jump-size bands.

definitions.name: jump measure
definitions.statement: For Borel B⊂R+×R, jX(ω,B)=Σ_{s>0}1_B(s,ΔXs(ω))1_{ΔXs(ω)≠0}; for cadlag X and A bounded away from zero, only finitely many A-jumps occur on each compact time interval.【修订 2026-10-06 R47】原文 Lemma 2（PDF p5）仅假设 A∈B*（0∉A），未写 bounded away from zero；数学上 0∉A 不足以保证结论（A={1/n} 可有无穷多 A-jumps），本卡条件是必要的数学修补而非原文转录，原文 p5 "A⊆R\(−ε,ε) for all ε>0" 的量词系原文疏漏（应为"存在 ε"）。
definitions.statement_original_r47: For Borel B⊂R+×R, jX(ω,B)=Σ_{s>0}1_B(s,ΔXs(ω))1_{ΔXs(ω)≠0}; for cadlag X and A bounded away from zero, only finitely many A-jumps occur on each compact time interval.

definitions.name: jump integrals on a finite-away-from-zero set
definitions.statement: For cadlag X, measurable f and Borel A⊂R with 0∉closure(A), the integral over [0,t]×A equals the pathwise sum over jump times and also over the iterative stopping-time labels; the absolute integral is bounded pathwise by a finite random maximum of |f| times the finite number of such jumps.

theorem_cards.label: Proposition 1 (iterative enumeration for cadlag adapted X)
assumptions: X is adapted and cadlag on a filtered probability space satisfying the usual conditions.

A is Borel and 0∉A.【修订 2026-10-06 R47（卡↔PDF 比对）】PDF p4 原文仅假设 0∉A；卡原句"hence is bounded away from zero"系错误推断（0∉A 推不出，反例 A={1/n}）。原文证明中 "lim ΔX_{t_n} ∈ Ā ⇒ ΔX_{t*}≠0 (since 0∉A)" 一步实际需要 0∉closure(A)（即 A 与 0 有正距离），该条件为闭合原文证明 gap 所需的附加假设，使用本命题时应显式补充；卡另一定义卡已用正确的 0∉closure(A) 表述。
theorem_cards.statement: Set T1A=inf{t>0:ΔXt∈A}, TnA=inf{t>Tn−1A:ΔXt∈A}; after modifying on an evanescent set, these are strictly increasing stopping times. The disjoint graphs of the adjusted SAn enumerate exactly {ΔX∈A}.
proof_steps: Use the standard stopping-time début result for cadlag adapted X.
Exclude finite accumulation of selected jumps: right continuity would force a nonzero limiting jump, contradicting the countability/regulated-path structure of the nonzero jump set.
If a selected jump time were not hit by the sequence, the next infimum would contradict the defining infimum; then apply the stopping-time graph theorem to obtain the disjoint graph union.
gaps: The iterative representation is for a fixed Borel jump-size set bounded away from zero; it does not by itself provide a nonhomogeneous compensator or an ordering rule for private frozen coordinates.
assumptions_original_r47: X is adapted and cadlag on a filtered probability space satisfying the usual conditions.
A is Borel and 0∉A, hence is bounded away from zero.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 4 (thin-set stopping-time enumeration for optional regulated X)
assumptions: X is optional; every trajectory is regulated; ΔX0=0.
Every trajectory has infinitely many jump times.
theorem_cards.statement: There is a sequence of stopping times (Tn) strictly increasing in (0,∞) for every ω such that the disjoint graphs [[Tn]] enumerate {ΔX≠0}; in particular the jump set is thin.
proof_steps: Show ΔX is optional from predictability of X− and optionality of X+.
For each path, partition its countable jump set into finite sets Dm by the regulated-path decomposition, and sort each Dm increasingly.
Each first element is the début of an optional set; subsequent elements are obtained after the optional interval after the preceding stopping time, hence are stopping times.
Reassemble the finite enumerations over m into a countable sequence; the infinite-jump assumption ensures the sequence can enumerate all jumps.
gaps: The pathwise infinite-jump condition excludes paths with only finitely many jumps; the theorem gives a measurable enumeration, not intensities or compensation identities.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 5 and Corollary 1 (induced integer-valued random measure)
assumptions: X is optional with regulated paths; ΔX0=0; every path has infinitely many jumps.
theorem_cards.statement: The function jX(ω,G)=Σ_{s>0}1_G(s,ΔXs(ω))1_{ΔXs(ω)≠0} is an integer-valued random measure, and its evaluation is the countable sum over the stopping-time enumeration from Theorem 4.
proof_steps: Invoke Theorem 4 to represent the thin jump set as disjoint stopping-time graphs.
Apply the cited random-measure theorem to obtain integer-valued measurability.
Substitute the disjoint graph indicators into the defining sum and interchange the two nonnegative sums.
gaps: This is an uncompensated jump measure. The paper ends by asking whether the finite-away-from-zero count and integral propositions extend to all optional regulated processes; those extensions are not claimed.

constant_dependence.explicit: No universal concentration constant is derived. For A bounded away from zero and finite t, the pathwise integral bound uses cAt(ω)=max_{jumps in [0,t]×A}|f(s,ΔXs)| and multiplies by jX(ω,[0,t]×A). For a Lévy process, the fixed-A count has Poisson intensity νX(A)=E[jX([0,1]×A)].
constant_dependence.dependence: The stopping-time construction depends on the chosen jump-size set A or on the countable pathwise magnitude/time decomposition; it does not yield a state/time-dependent intensity λ(t,x) or a compensator ν.

endpoint_limits.small_jumps: The finite-count and finite-integral claims require jump sizes separated from zero; infinitely many small jumps are not covered by those finite-sum statements.
endpoint_limits.optional_regulated: The paper extends graph enumeration and the random-measure definition, but explicitly leaves open whether the finite-count and integration propositions hold for arbitrary optional regulated trajectories.
endpoint_limits.compensation: No Doob–Meyer/random-measure compensator is constructed for general X; the Lévy Poisson statement is a special law of the uncompensated count, not a general compensation theorem.
endpoint_limits.iteration: No coordinate freezing, state update, intensity iteration, or convergence/error estimate is defined.

reusable_methods.method: Enumerate cadlag jumps in a Borel size band by successive first-hit stopping times
reusable_methods.transfer: If the target process has cadlag adapted paths and its selected jump sizes stay away from zero, the same pathwise/filtration check can support event labeling. It does not establish target intensity or compensation.

reusable_methods.method: Enumerate optional regulated jump graphs via finite pathwise layers and début stopping times
reusable_methods.transfer: Could provide a measurable jump-label layer if the target state process is optional regulated and has infinitely many jumps on every path, but those hypotheses and enumeration order must be proved for the target.
